THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Chili Mac and Cheese

Adjusted recipe for 4 servings. Use the ingredient quantities below.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME35 min
COOK METHODOne pot
EST. / SERVING~380 cal | ~39g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: TWO POTS FOR THE PASTA. Carbe Diem elbows in one, Barilla regular in the other. Salt both. Cook per package. Non-negotiable — this is the split.

Ingredients scaled from the original 8-serving recipe. Cooking times, pan size, and amounts written in the method may need adjustment.

Ingredients

SAUCE BASE (blended, then split 2:1)

  • ~150 g cottage cheese
  • 1/4 cup fat-free Fairlife ultra-filtered milk
  • 1 tbsp nutritional yeast
  • 1 tbsp cheddar cheese powder

LOOSENER

  • 0.2 cup Kirkland chicken bone broth (1/4 cup adult pot + 1/8 cup kid pot)

ADULT PASTA

  • 4 oz dry Carbe Diem elbows (or Pete's higher-fiber elbows) — 2 oz per adult container

ADULT MELT

  • 1 oz Velveeta Original

Option 1

  • 3 oz dry Barilla regular elbows — 1.5 oz per kid container
  • 1 full-serving equivalents Hot Dog Chili Base (~140-160 g total = 1/2 serving per container)
  • 1/2 oz Velveeta Original
  • 0.1 cup Kirkland chicken bone broth

CHAIN-FROM (from cookbook)

  • 3 servings prepared Hot Dog Chili Base (~420-480 g total — the reserve from Chili Hot Dogs)

MELT

  • 1 1/2 oz Velveeta Original (2 oz adult pot + 1 oz kid pot)

SEASONING

  • Salt (for both pasta waters)

ADULT PORTION

  • 2 full servings Hot Dog Chili Base (~280-320 g total)

ADULT LOOSENER

  • 0.1 cup Kirkland chicken bone broth

Allergens: gluten, dairy, mustard, fish. Possible soy

AT THE PASTA + THE POT. Two pastas cooked in two pots. Sauce blended once, then divided 2:1 into adult and kid pots. Velveeta + chili + bone broth added to each pot per its portion.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.BLEND THE SAUCE BASE. Cottage cheese + Fairlife into a blender until mostly smooth. Add nutritional yeast + cheddar powder. Blend again until completely smooth and pourable. If curd texture remains, blend 60 sec more.
  2. 2.TWO POTS, TWO PASTAS. Cook 8 oz Carbe Diem elbows (adult) and 6 oz Barilla regular elbows (kid) in separate salted-water pots per each pasta's package directions. Drain both, return to their original pots.
  3. 3.DIVIDE THE SAUCE 2. 1: Two parts of the blended sauce into the adult pot, one part into the kid pot. Adult pot carries more pasta and gets more sauce.
  4. 4.MELT VELVEETA. 2 oz Velveeta into the adult pot + 1 oz into the kid pot. Stir over LOW heat until fully melted and glossy. Do NOT add the chili yet — Velveeta needs bare pasta + sauce to melt cleanly.
  5. 5.ADD RESERVED CHILI. 4 full servings (~280-320 g) of Hot Dog Chili Base into the adult pot. 2 full-serving equivalents (~140-160 g) into the kid pot — this becomes half a chili serving in each of the 4 kid containers. Fold to combine.
  6. 6.LOOSEN + FOLD. 1/4 cup bone broth into the adult pot, 1/8 cup into the kid pot. Fold over low heat until creamy and evenly combined. Sauce should coat the pasta glossy, not pool.
  7. 7.PORTION 4+4 CONTAINERS. Divide the adult pot across 4 airtight containers (~2 oz dry pasta + 1 chili serving + one-quarter of the adult sauce build per container). Divide the kid pot across 4 airtight containers. Cool 20-30 min uncovered before sealing — critical for texture across the week.

Adult — Carbe Diem Higher-Fiber Elbows + Full Chili Serving

  1. 8.ADULT CONTAINER = 2 oz dry Carbe Diem elbows cooked + 1 full chili serving + one-quarter of the adult pot's sauce build + 1/2 oz Velveeta melt-in equivalent. ~380 cal / 39g protein per container.

Kid — Barilla Regular Elbows + Half Chili Serving (Same Sauce Base) · Option 1

  1. 8.KID POT. 1.5 oz dry Barilla regular elbows + one-third of the blended sauce + 1 oz Velveeta melted in + 2 full-serving equivalents of Hot Dog Chili Base folded through + 1/8 cup bone broth. Fold until creamy.
  2. 9.PORTION 4 KID CONTAINERS. Divide the kid pot across 4 airtight containers. Each container ≈ 1.5 oz dry pasta + 1/2 chili serving + one-quarter of the kid sauce build. Cool 20-30 min uncovered before sealing.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Carbe Diem Higher-Fiber Elbows + Full Chili Serving: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Barilla Regular Elbows + Half Chili Serving (Same Sauce Base): Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • BLEND THE COTTAGE CHEESE UNTIL POURABLE. Blender with cottage cheese + Fairlife until smooth. Then add nutritional yeast + cheddar powder. Blend again. If it still shows curd texture, blend longer.
  • DIVIDE SAUCE 2:1. Two parts to the adult pot (which has 8 oz dry pasta / 4 servings). One part to the kid pot (which has 6 oz dry pasta / 4 servings). Kid gets less sauce because kid pasta is a smaller portion.

If something fails

Cottage cheese sauce is grainy / curdy: Not blended enough. Return to blender with 2 tbsp more Fairlife and blend 60 sec more until pourable. Cheddar powder + nutritional yeast can also mask residual curd — add them last, blend again.

Velveeta didn't melt cleanly / has flecks: Chili went in too early. Velveeta needs bare pasta + hot sauce to melt. Next time: pasta → sauce → Velveeta (melt over LOW heat, stir) → chili → broth. Rescue: warm the whole pot over low with 2 tbsp more Fairlife, whisk gently. Flecks may partially melt back in.

Adult pasta feels dry / stiff by day 3: Pete's/Carbe Diem protein pastas tighten in the fridge as they absorb sauce. Add a 2 tbsp splash of milk or bone broth before reheating; cover the container while microwaving. Same technique keeps id 41 Beef Bacon Pasta creamy across the week.

Kid rejects the fiber-elbow chew: Kid was fed the adult pasta by mistake. Kid pot is Barilla regular elbows only; adult pot is Carbe Diem only. Check labels before pouring — the split is the whole macro-hack.

Sauce reads flat / not cheesy enough: Skipped or under-dosed the cheddar powder + nutritional yeast. Add another 1 tbsp cheddar powder + 1 tbsp yeast, blend or fold in. That's what makes it read as chili MAC, not creamy chili pasta.

Containers went soggy overnight: Sealed hot. Steam under a warm lid softens the pasta. Cool 20-30 min uncovered before sealing — critical step for meal-prep pastas of any kind.

Out of Hot Dog Chili Base reserve: This dinner is designed as the second half of the Chili Hot Dogs chain. Starting fresh means a full 25-30 min chili base cook (see the Hot Dog Chili Base cookbook page). Or sub any thick, no-bean beef chili — Amy's, Wolf Brand, or homemade.

Storage and reheating

Store: Portion into 8 airtight containers (4 adult + 4 kid). Cool 20-30 min uncovered before sealing — critical step to prevent lid steam from softening the pasta. Refrigerate promptly.

Reheat: Microwave covered 90 sec + a 2 tbsp splash of milk or bone broth if the sauce has tightened, stir, 30 more sec. Reheat to 165°F. Stovetop reheat on low with a splash of broth preserves texture best; microwave is acceptable.

Lasts: 3-4 days fridge. Cottage cheese + Velveeta blend holds better than heavy-cream Alfredo across the week — same pattern as id 41 Beef Bacon Pasta. Freezing is possible but the dairy sauce may soften or separate slightly after thawing; best fresh through day 3.

Chili Mac and Cheese

The chili from Chili Hot Dogs is the T3 lever. 6 reserved servings + a blended cottage-cheese-and-Velveeta sauce + two pastas (Carbe Diem for adults, Barilla regular for kids) = 8 meal-prep containers that don't taste like a leftover repeat. 35 min end-to-end.

Make this when

You cooked Chili Hot Dogs earlier in the week and reserved 6 servings of the 12-serving Hot Dog Chili Base. This dinner cashes in the reserve — 8 meal-prep containers, ~380 cal / 39g protein per adult container, ready to reheat all week. One chili base = two family dinners without a second cook.

Brands I use

Hot Dog Chili Base
Cookbook cross-link — the reusable component this dinner chains from
This dinner IS the second half of the Chili Hot Dogs chain. Cook one 12-serving base for the Chili Hot Dogs dinner earlier in the week; the 6 reserved servings feed the 8 Chili Mac containers here. Full method + macros on the cookbook page.
Split Plate Chili Hot Dogs
Recipe cross-link — the first dinner in the chain
The narrative pair. Cook Chili Hot Dogs (id 51) on chili-dog night, plate the family, then reserve the remaining 6 chili servings. Chili Mac becomes the next-day 8-container meal prep — no second cook, no repeat-feel.
Carbe Diem
Higher-fiber elbows (adult carb — ~17g protein / 7g net carbs per serving)
The adult macro anchor. Higher-fiber elbow pasta lets the sauce stay full-fat (Velveeta + cottage cheese) while adult macros stay honest at 380 cal / 39g protein. Sub Pete's higher-fiber elbows or Barilla Protein+ elbows.
Barilla
Regular Elbows (kid carb — familiar shape + soft cook)
Kids reject the fiber-elbow chew. Kid pot uses Barilla regular so the pasta reads as normal mac-and-cheese texture. Sub any small elbow-cut wheat pasta.
Velveeta
Original slices (2 oz adult pot + 1 oz kid pot melt)
Tier 2 melt anchor. Melts cleanly into hot pasta + cottage-cheese sauce in seconds. Locks the mac-and-cheese identity. Sub American slices for a shorter ingredient list.
Fairlife
Fat-free Ultra-Filtered Milk (sauce thinner)
Lactose-free, high-protein, low-carb. Blends into the cottage cheese to make a pourable sauce. Not dairy-free.
